new_records.title: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master's (CGRS-M)
new_records.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master's program provides financial support to high-calibre scholars engaged in an eligible master's or, in some cases, doctoral program in Canada. Part of the harmonized Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS).
new_records.official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students
Enrolled or intending to enroll in a full-time eligible master's program at a Canadian institution
Meet the specific agency mandate (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
Have not exceeded lifetime maximum of tri-agency support
new_records.eligibility_summary: Open to domestic and international students in full-time master's programs at Canadian institutions, subject to agency-specific research mandates.
benefits: Can be held at any eligible Canadian university
requirements: Application through CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC portal
Research proposal aligned with agency mandate
application_method: Apply directly to CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC online portal
new_records.selection_notes: Merit-based; evaluated by agency-specific peer review committees.
new_records.best_fit: High-calibre master's students seeking research funding across all disciplines.
new_records.notes: Replaces the former CGS-M program under the harmonized CRTAS suite. International students are eligible through all three agencies.

new_records.title: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS-D)
new_records.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral program recognizes and supports the next generation of outstanding innovators and researchers. Part of the harmonized Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS).
new_records.official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students
Enrolled or intending to enroll in a full-time eligible doctoral program at a Canadian institution
Meet the specific agency mandate (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
Have not previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC

benefits: Eligible for affiliated fellowships and supplements
requirements: Application through CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC portal

application_method: Apply directly to CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC online portal
new_records.selection_notes: Merit-based; evaluated by agency-specific peer review committees. Automatically considered for affiliated fellowships at some institutions.
new_records.best_fit: Outstanding doctoral students pursuing research careers across all disciplines.
new_records.notes: Replaces the former CGSD program under the harmonized CRTAS suite. Distinct from the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship.

new_records.title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS)
new_records.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) is a merit-based scholarship program jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and Ontario universities. It supports outstanding graduate students in all disciplines of academic study.
new_records.application_period: University-specific internal deadlines; provincial competition annually
new_records.official_source: School of Graduate Studies, University of Toronto / Ontario Ministry of Colleges, Universities, Research Excellence and Security
eligibility: Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, Protected Persons
International students with a valid study permit by the university deadline
Enrolled or intending to enroll full-time in an eligible master's or doctoral program at an Ontario university
Minimum A- average in last two academic years
Must not have exceeded lifetime maximum of government-funded student awards
new_records.eligibility_summary: Open to domestic and international graduate students at participating Ontario universities with strong academic records.
coverage: Living stipend: up to $15,000 per year
requirements: Apply through the participating Ontario university
Research proposal or statement of intent
application_method: Submit application to the Ontario university where you plan to hold the award
new_records.selection_notes: University-specific internal deadlines apply. Applications are first adjudicated at the university level, then forwarded to a centralized provincial competition.
new_records.best_fit: Graduate students with strong academic records seeking merit-based funding at Ontario universities.

new_records.title: Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship (AGES)

eligibility: Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, Protected Persons
International students with a valid study permit

new_records.title: Quebec Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students (PBEEE)

new_records.title: Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA)
new_records.description: The Canada Postdoctoral Research Award program is a federal research talent investment program in the Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS), jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC, and SSHRC. It replaces the former Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships and agency-specific postdoctoral fellowships.
new_records.deadline_display: CIHR: September 16, 2026; NSERC: October 17, 2026; SSHRC: September 10, 2026
new_records.official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international applicants
Hold (or expect to hold) a doctorate or health professional degree before award start date
Not hold or be on leave from a tenure-track or tenured faculty position

Cannot have previously received a tri-agency postdoctoral award
Cannot hold a CPRA concurrently with another tri-agency research training award
Apply to only one agency per year (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
new_records.eligibility_summary: Outstanding postdoctoral researchers of all nationalities who have completed their PhD within the last three years and are not in tenured faculty positions.

new_records.best_fit: Top-tier postdoctoral researchers seeking advanced research training in Canada.
new_records.notes: Replaces the Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships and former CIHR/NSERC/SSHRC postdoctoral fellowships. Maximum three lifetime applications permitted.
